tests.name: MHPCO Claim Office quotes an empty item list -- premium 5 G (processing fee only)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes a single plain sword -- base 100 G + 10 G first insurance + 5 G fee = 115 G
MHPCO Claim Office quotes a single plain amulet -- base 60 G + 6 G first insurance + 5 G fee = 71 G
MHPCO Claim Office quotes a single plain staff -- base 80 G + 8 G first insurance + 5 G fee = 93 G
MHPCO Claim Office quotes a single plain potion -- base 40 G + 4 G first insurance + 5 G fee = 49 G
MHPCO Claim Office quotes a single rune -- base 25 G component premium -> 33 G
MHPCO Claim Office quotes a single moonstone -- base 25 G component premium -> 33 G
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 2 runes -- base premium 50 G (no block) -> 60 G
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 3 runes -- base premium 60 G (block applies) -> 71 G
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 4 runes -- base premium 100 G (no block; block requires exactly 3) -> 115 G
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 7 runes -- base premium 175 G (no block at 7) -> 198 G
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 2 runes + 1 moonstone -- base premium 75 G (no block: different types) -> 88 G
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 3 runes + 3 moonstones -- base premium 120 G (two separate blocks) -> 137 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies the 50% curse surcharge to the cursed item's base premium -- cursed sword base 100 G -> 150 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies the 30% high-enchantment surcharge at enchantment exactly 5 -- sword base 100 G -> 130 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies no high-enchantment surcharge at enchantment 4 -- sword base premium stays 100 G -> 115 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies both curse and high-enchantment surcharges to a cursed sword with enchantment exactly 5 -- 100 + 50 + 30 = 180 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies the curse surcharge only to the cursed item on a multi-item policy -- cursed sword + plain amulet: base 160 G + 50 G curse = 210 G before further modifiers and fee
MHPCO Claim Office applies the 20% loyalty discount at exactly 2 years with MHPCO -- policy base 100 G -> -20 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies no loyalty discount at 1 year with MHPCO
MHPCO Claim Office applies the 10% first-insurance surcharge to the policy base premium
MHPCO Claim Office applies the 15% follow-up discount on each contract after the customer's first quote
MHPCO Claim Office applies no follow-up discount on the customer's first quote
MHPCO Claim Office applies the first-insurance surcharge on a follow-up contract too -- each quoted item is a first insurance regardless of customer history
MHPCO Claim Office rounds a premium of 197.5 G up to 198 G (MHPCO's favour)
MHPCO Claim Office keeps intermediate premium amounts as fractions and rounds only the final premium
MHPCO Claim Office quotes newcomer with a cursed steel sword (enchantment 3), 0 years -- premium 165 G
MHPCO Claim Office quotes long-standing customer's second contract, cursed steel sword (enchantment 7), 3 years -- premium 160 G
MHPCO Claim Office rejects a quote containing an unknown item type (e.g. broomstick) -- domain layer throws; the CLI turns that into a non-zero exit with stderr output
MHPCO Claim Office caps a single-sword policy at 2000 G -- insurance sum 1000 G, cap = 2 x sum
MHPCO Claim Office computes the insurance sum of a staff + potion policy as 1200 G -- staff 800 + potion 400
MHPCO Claim Office computes the insurance sum of a sword + amulet policy as 1600 G -- cap 3200 G
MHPCO Claim Office computes the insurance sum of two swords as 2000 G -- cap 4000 G
MHPCO Claim Office computes the insurance sum of a sword + 3 runes as 1750 G -- the block discount affects the premium only, cap 3500 G
MHPCO Claim Office bases the cap on the unmodified insurance value -- cursed sword (premium 165 G) still has cap 2000 G
MHPCO Claim Office pays 400 G for a regular steel sword (enchantment 3) with damage 500 G -- full reimbursement minus 100 G deductible
MHPCO Claim Office pays 100 G for a damaged rune (no enchantment, no material) with damage 200 G -- 200 - 100 deductible
MHPCO Claim Office applies the 100 G deductible once per damaged item -- sword 500 G + amulet 300 G in one incident = payout 600 G
MHPCO Claim Office reimburses 50% for damage to an item with enchantment exactly 8 -- dragon sword, damage 1000 G -> payout 400 G
MHPCO Claim Office fully reimburses damage to a dragon-material item -- dragon sword enchantment 5, damage 800 G -> payout 700 G
MHPCO Claim Office prefers the 50% high-enchantment rule over full dragon reimbursement -- dragon sword enchantment 9, damage 1000 G -> payout 400 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies only the high-enchantment clause to a steel sword enchantment 9, damage 1000 G -> payout 400 G
MHPCO Claim Office pays 1400 G and leaves cap remaining 600 G for the first 1500 G claim on a sword policy (cap 2000 G)
MHPCO Claim Office reduces the second 1500 G claim to the remaining cap -- payout 600 G, cap remaining 0 G
MHPCO Claim Office treats each damage entry of a repeated item type as a separate damage with its own deductible -- two swords, two sword damages
MHPCO Claim Office rejects a claim with more damage entries of a type than the policy covers -- domain layer throws; the CLI turns that into a non-zero exit with stderr output
MHPCO Claim Office rounds a payout of 350.5 G down to 350 G (MHPCO's favour)

MHPCO Claim Office rejects a claim referencing an item not covered by the policy (amulet damaged, only a sword insured) -- domain layer throws; the CLI turns that into a non-zero exit with stderr output
MHPCO Claim Office rejects a claim referencing an unknown item type -- domain layer throws; the CLI turns that into a non-zero exit with stderr output
MHPCO Claim Office rejects a claim with a negative damage amount (-200) -- domain layer throws; the CLI turns that into a non-zero exit with stderr output
MHPCO Claim Office reads a scenario from stdin and writes {results: [...]} to stdout in step order
MHPCO Claim Office resolves a claim step's policy field as the zero-based index of the quote step that created the policy
MHPCO Claim Office runs the schema example end to end -- amulet quote then 200 G amulet claim -> premium and payout/remainingCap
claim-office CLI reads a scenario from stdin and writes the results as JSON to stdout
claim-office CLI exits non-zero and writes an error to stderr for an unknown item type, with no results on stdout
